title: Fragment coordination, tool-proxy degradation modes, and acceptance criteria for streamed structured outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: define hardened acceptance criteria and operational behavior for streamed structured outputs that include delegated tool/function invocations. This ticket codifies the handshake, fragmenting and reassembly rules, error taxonomy, and allowed fallbacks when the tool-proxy path degrades or is unavailable. Goal is to ship a deterministic contract that client SDKs and runtime can implement consistently and that operators can use to diagnose degradations without data loss or silent corruption.
scope_change: Initial PRD assumed best-effort tool proxy retries. Scope clarified 2026-02-26: must include explicit 'proxy-degraded' behavior with three fallback modes (soft-summary, queued-execution, synchronous-fallback) selectable by customer policy. Also added requirement for per-request idempotency tokens and checkpoint frames for resumability. Removed synchronous-only retry path for long-running tool calls to avoid blocking low-latency clients.
acceptance_criteria: Envelope framing: every streamed session MUST emit a single root 'envelope' JSON object and MAY emit 'fragment' frames. Envelope includes: session_id, format_version, model_version, schema_id, and correlation_id.

Fragment ordering and sequence checks: each fragment MUST include sequence_number and total_fragments when known. Runtime MUST validate monotonic sequence numbers and flag missing sequences in a 'fragment_gap' metric and error frame.

Checkpoint frames: runtime MUST emit checkpoint frames at configurable intervals (default: every 3 fragments or every 1s), each checkpoint includes continuation_token that is safe to persist and use to resume without duplication when paired with idempotency_token.

Idempotency and resume: every request that may invoke tools MUST accept an idempotency_token. Using the same token + continuation_token to resume MUST produce deterministic reassembly and NOT re-invoke completed tool calls.

Tool-proxy degradation modes: when the tool proxy is slow or failing, runtime MUST support three policy-driven fallbacks: 'soft-summary' (emit textual summary of intended tool result and mark tool_call.status=degraded), 'queued-execution' (acknowledge to client that tool call is queued and emit placeholder with queued_id), 'synchronous-fallback' (attempt local minimal impl if available). Behavior MUST be configurable per-project and per-route.

Error taxonomy mapping: errors MUST be classified into: transient (RETRYABLE), permanent (FAILED), partial (PARTIAL_RESULT), and degradation (DEGRADED_PROXY). Each streamed frame that terminates with a non-success MUST include error_code (string), error_class (one of the above), human_message, and optional remediation_hint.

Partial-object semantics: when a fragment contains a partial object, the runtime MUST emit a 'partial_object' marker and guarantee that the final assembled object conforms to declared schema_id or else emit a schema_violation event and trigger configured rollback behavior.

Backpressure signaling: when internal queue/backlog exceeds threshold, runtime MUST emit a 'PAUSE' control-frame to the client and expose metrics (backpressure_rate, avg_queue_ms). Clients SHOULD back off and optionally use a retry-after provided in the PAUSE frame.

Observability: events and metrics for each session MUST include fragment_count, fragments_missing, fragment_reassembly_time_ms, tool_call_latency_ms, tool_proxy_retry_count, degrade_mode_activated, resume_success_count, and sample traces linked by correlation_id.

Testing: end-to-end conformance suite MUST pass including fuzzed fragment loss (simulate up to 30% fragment drop), out-of-order delivery, duplicate fragments, tool-proxy timeouts, and network partition. Recovery tests MUST validate no double-invocation for idempotent tool calls.

Telemetry retention for incident triage: traces for degraded sessions MUST be retained for 30 days in the default plan and 90 days for enterprise customers (configurable). Logs MUST include sanitized request prompts and tool metadata; sensitive tokens MUST be redacted per security policy.

SDK compatibility: JS/Go/Python SDKs MUST implement reassembly and checkpoint resume APIs and expose policy knobs for fallback mode and checkpoint frequency. Backwards compatibility: if client omits format_version, runtime MUST default to v1-compat behavior for 6 months then log deprecation warnings.

Operator playbook: when 'degrade_mode_activated' is seen >1% of sessions in 5m, alert on-call with runbook steps: (1) query proxy health dashboard link, (2) toggle soft-summary off, (3) scale proxy pool, (4) if persistent, enable queued-execution for critical tenants. Playbook MUST be linked from console incident action.

Security: tool-call payloads routed to external proxies MUST be encrypted in transit and use per-request ephemeral keys when possible. Any policy that enables queued-execution MUST ensure KMS encryption for queued payloads at rest. Security review signed-off required before GA.

GA criteria: no critical or P0 regressions in 2-week canary with 5 enterprise customers and synthetic workloads including high fragment-rate and tool-heavy traffic. Observability thresholds for fragment_loss_rate <0.1% and resume_success_rate >99.5%.
Documentation: PRD, SDK docs, and operator playbook MUST be published prior to GA with examples for three fallback modes and a migration guide for customers using older streaming formats.
test_plan: Conformance runner: implement 120 tests in the streaming-conformance repo covering message loss, reorder, duplication, corrupt frames, and resume via continuation_token.
Chaos tests: network partition simulator with tool proxy instances; assert no double-invocations under idempotency tokens and validate queued-execution ordering guarantees.
Load test: sustained 10k fragments/sec across a mix of short and long-running tool calls. Monitor backpressure metrics and ensure tail latency SLOs remain within target.
Security validation: threat model review, KMS integration test for queued payloads, and redaction checks in logs and traces.
SDK e2e: test JS/Go/Python clients for resume, checkpointing, PAUSE handling, and fallback policy toggles against local test harness.
Manual acceptance: product sign-off checklist: PRD review, two design approvals, one architecture review, and successful canary deployment report attached.
Regression suite: run streaming-negatives and structured-schema-tests against previous release to ensure no regressions in format parsing.
decisions: Use envelope + framed fragments rather than length-prefixed raw JSON to simplify partial object semantics and make control frames explicit (decided 2026-02-22).
Introduce continuation_token that encodes server-side durable pointer; token format will be opaque to clients to allow internal evolution (decided 2026-02-26).
Require idempotency_token for any request that routes to a tool proxy; server will reject tool-invoking requests without token after grace period.
Expose three fallback modes and make them configurable at route and tenant level; default will be 'soft-summary' for public tiers.
